entries.content:
Synora = Vietnamese voice-AI companion + plant-care device on **ESP32-S3 N16R8**
(16MB flash, 8MB octal PSRAM). See [[project_firmware_greenfield]] and
[[project_ble_always_on]].

**Finalized sensor/peripheral suite (decided 2026-07-23, SUPERSEDED — see config.h comments as of 2026-09-19):**
current `firmware-synora/main/boards/synora/config.h` shows the opposite of
both swaps below: **DHT11** (not SHT31, GPIO9 single-wire) and **VL53L1X**
(not L0X, its own I2C_NUM_1 bus) are what's actually wired/coded now — SHT31
and the L0X downgrade were apparently reverted at some point after this note
was written. Don't trust this paragraph; check config.h directly.

I2C bus (shared, SDA=GPIO9 / SCL=GPIO8):
- **SHT31** air temp/humidity, addr 0x44 — NEW, **replaces DHT11** (frees GPIO17).
- **VL53L0X** ToF water-tank level, addr 0x29 — **downgraded from VL53L1X** to cut cost.
- ~~BH1750 ambient light~~ — considered, **DROPPED for v1** (2026-07-23; mounting/backlight-spill
  hassle not worth it yet). If revived: I2C 0x23, top-mount facing up, baffle from TFT/LED,
  DLI = integrate lux over time (one sensor is enough).

ADC (GPIO1 = ADC1_CH0):
- **Capacitive** soil-moisture sensor — **replaces the resistive LM393** module
  (resistive probes corrode/drift). Needs its own dry/wet calibration.

Audio: INMP441 mic (I2S, WS41/SCK39/DIN40, L/R->GND), MAX98357A amp (BCLK6/LRCK7/DOUT5).
Other: water pump via IRLZ44N MOSFET (GPIO47), status LED (GPIO48), 18650 2P
battery + charging, low-batt warning. (A second TTP223 "AI call button" on
GPIO2 was planned but removed 2026-08-03 as dead code -- the single BOOT
button already covers factory-reset-hold + voice-session-toggle-click, no
second button needed.)

**Display swapped 2026-08-03: ST7735S SPI 128x128 -> Open-Smart 3.5" ST7793,
240x400, 8-bit parallel (I80).** Product listing said "240x480" -- wrong;
240x400 is what the chip's own register map and vendor reference driver
actually use (432 gate lines is the chip's hard max, not what this panel
wires). No ESP-IDF component exists for ST7793 (checked the registry);
`synora_display.cc` drives it with a hand-rolled register-level init ported
from the module's own TFT_eSPI reference driver (`demo_ST7793.zip`), talking
to `esp_lcd_panel_io` directly rather than through an `esp_lcd_panel_handle_t`.

**2026-09-22: display swapped again, ST7793 240x400 I80 -> ILI9341 240x320
4-wire SPI (portrait).** Unlike ST7793, ILI9341 has a real esp_lcd vendor
component (`espressif/esp_lcd_ili9341 ^2.1.0`), so `synora_display.cc` now
goes through a normal `esp_lcd_panel_handle_t`
(`esp_lcd_new_panel_ili9341()` + `esp_lcd_panel_reset/init/draw_bitmap()`)
instead of hand-rolled register writes. Pins: CS=GPIO10, DC=GPIO11,
RST=GPIO12, SCK=GPIO13, MOSI=GPIO14 (reused from the old parallel ribbon's
first 5 pins; GPIO16-18/21/38/42 freed up). Backlight tied to 3V3, not a
GPIO. All UI layout constants in `synora_display.cc` were also rescaled for
the shorter 320-tall canvas (was 400) -- eyes/mouth moved up, dashboard grid
+ footer compressed, pairing-screen QR moved above the hint text instead of
below.

Real-hardware bring-up gotchas found this session (none of this was
predictable from the datasheet/code alone -- all confirmed via actual
flashing + a photo of the panel):
- **20MHz SPI clock caused torn/garbled frames** over jumper-wire wiring.
  Dropped `io_config.pclk_hz` to 10MHz in `InitializePanel()`; can likely be
  raised once the wiring is soldered/shortened, but untested.
- **Pushing the full 240x320 framebuffer (153600 bytes) as one
  `esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap()` call caused `E spi_master:
  setup_dma_priv_buffer: Failed to allocate priv TX buffer` and silently
  partial/noisy frames.** Root cause: `framebuffer_` lives in PSRAM
  (`MALLOC_CAP_DMA | MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM`), so the SPI driver bounces each
  transfer through a temporary *internal*-DRAM buffer -- a single
  153600-byte bounce allocation competes with WiFi/BT/esp-sr/audio for that
  same limited internal RAM and fails. Fixed by chunking `PushFramebuffer()`
  into 40-row bands (240*40*2 = 19200 bytes/transfer, 8 bands total) --
  small enough to reliably allocate alongside those subsystems. If display
  corruption/noise ever reappears after adding more RAM-hungry features,
  suspect this same internal-DRAM contention first and consider shrinking
  `kBandHeight` further before anything else.
- **This specific ILI9341 module's default orientation needed both
  `esp_lcd_panel_swap_xy(panel_, true)` AND `esp_lcd_panel_mirror(panel_,
  true, true)`** (a full 180-degree-rotated-from-landscape correction) to
  read right-side-up in portrait -- confirmed by photographing the panel
  mid-bring-up (text was legible but running along the wrong axis, then
  rotated 180 after swap_xy alone). Don't assume a future ILI9341 module
  needs the same flags -- this varies per module/glass orientation and must
  be re-derived from a real photo, not guessed from documentation.
- `rgb_ele_order = LCD_RGB_ELEMENT_ORDER_BGR` and `invert_color(false)` were
  both first-guess defaults that turned out correct on this module (no color
  complaints after the orientation fix) -- don't second-guess these unless
  colors actually look wrong on hardware.
- Sandbox environment note: `managed_components/` and the default `build/`
  dir had several subdirectories left root-owned from an earlier `sudo
  idf.py build` run, which silently breaks the component manager (`rmtree`
  `PermissionError`) the next time `idf_component.yml` changes and deps need
  re-resolving. Fixed with `sudo chown -R toan:toan managed_components`;
  built into a fresh `build2/` dir rather than fighting the old `build/`'s
  permissions. If `idf.py build` fails with a `PermissionError` inside
  `managed_components/` or `build/log/`, check ownership before assuming a
  real dependency problem.
- Also in this sandbox: the `rtk` hook wrapper intercepts plain `find` (and
  presumably other common commands) and silently mishandles compound
  predicates like `-not`/`-exec` (returns empty/wrong results instead of
  erroring loudly) -- cost real time confirming which `managed_components`
  dirs were root-owned. Use `/usr/bin/find` (or `rtk proxy find ...`) instead
  of bare `find` when the exact output matters for debugging.

Hardware gotchas that cost real debugging time (all resolved, see
`firmware-synora/main/boards/synora/wiring.md` for the full pin table):
- **GPIO19/20 are the ESP32-S3's fixed native-USB D-/D+ pins.** Using them
  for anything else (display data lines, originally) makes the board crash
  and drop off USB the moment that peripheral initializes.
- **GPIO22-25 don't exist on the ESP32-S3 at all** (valid range: 0-21, 26-48).
  Assigning them (to pump/LED, originally) goes undetected until something
  actually references the macro in code -- fails to compile only then.
- **This module's backlight (LED) pin is active-low** -- wire it to GND, not
  3.3V/VCC like the usual convention on similar modules. Confirmed via diode
  test (LEDs were healthy, just wired backwards) + hardware trial.
- **esp_lcd's i80 driver auto-swizzles (byte-swaps) `tx_param`'s param buffer
  whenever `lcd_param_bits > bus_width`** (ours: 16 > 8), unconditionally,
  regardless of the `swap_color_bytes` flag (that flag only governs
  `tx_color`). Manually pre-swapping register-value bytes on top of that
  double-swaps and corrupts every register write -- silently produces a
  stable-but-wrong panel state (uniform white, no crash) rather than an
  obvious failure. Pass values in natural host byte order and let the
  automatic swizzle handle it.
- Also fixed in the same pass: a pre-existing `WifiManager::Initialize()`
  call missing from `SynoraBoard`'s constructor caused a `tcpip_send_msg_
  wait_sem`/`Invalid mbox` crash loop whenever `SynoraMqtt::EnsureStarted()`
  ran for an already-provisioned device -- unrelated to the display work,
  found while chasing a crash/USB-drop symptom that turned out to be the
  GPIO19/20 conflict instead.
- **2026-08-03: `WifiManager::GetInstance().StartStation()` was only ever
  called from inside `BleProvisioning::Init()`, which `SynoraBoard`'s
  constructor deliberately skips for an already-paired device** -- so a
  returning/rebooted paired device's WiFi station never actually connected
  (driver initialized, but never scanned/associated). Looked exactly like a
  DNS problem (`esp-tls: couldn't get hostname ... getaddrinfo() returns
  202`/`EAI_FAIL`) since every network call failed the same way, and a
  Cloudflare/Google DNS-fallback override was tried first -- the real fix
  was calling `StartStation()` unconditionally in `SynoraBoard`'s
  constructor. Confirmed via a full boot log: `WifiManager` logged
  "Initialized" and then nothing else WiFi-related ever again (no
  "Connecting to WiFi"/"Got IP" lines at all).
- The UART test console (`test_console.cc`, `esp_console` REPL with
  `help`/`telemetry`/`fonttest`/`dns` commands) binds to the native
  USB-Serial-JTAG peripheral (`/dev/ttyACM0`), not UART0 -- UART0's
  physical routing on this board (via an ST-Link VCP on `/dev/ttyACM1`) was
  never confirmed reachable in either direction, while ttyACM0 is the same
  port already used all session for flashing/log monitoring.

**Firmware implications for Phase 3 (all decisions differ from the current fork's config.h):**
- Board driver must use a **VL53L0X** library, NOT the `saleca/vl53l1x_uld_esp_wrapper`
  component the fork uses — different API. (ToF-on-water caveat: a calm water
  surface is a weak/specular IR reflector; L0X has less signal margin than L1X.
  Mount perpendicular, validate on hardware.)
- Swap DHT11 driver -> SHT31 (I2C); add BH1750 driver. Both ride the existing I2C bus.
- Recalibrate soil moisture for the capacitive module (different dry/wet range).
- Skipped: LD2410 presence sensor (no companion presence sensing in v1).
- Three I2C sensors + ToF on one bus: addresses 0x23/0x44/0x29 don't conflict; keep
  4.7k pull-ups adequate for the added bus capacitance.

**2026-08-03: Real TTS implemented, voice pipeline now fully real end-to-end.**
Server-side (`server/`), not firmware: added a `tts/` sidecar, mirroring
`asr/`'s Python-sidecar-on-compose-network pattern, alongside the
pre-existing `asr/` (PhoWhisper STT, already real before this).
`LlmVoicePipeline` calls a real `ITextToSpeech` and Opus-encodes the result
(`OpusAudioDecoder.EncodeToOpusFrames`, new) instead of echoing the user's
own recording back -- that echo fallback still exists, but only fires if
the TTS call itself fails.

TTS backend was swapped same day: started with facebook/mms-tts-vie
(VITS via `transformers.VitsModel`) -- single-speaker, no voice choice,
16kHz native (conveniently matched the pipeline's fixed rate). Replaced
with **VieNeu-TTS v3 Turbo** (`pnnbao-ump/VieNeu-TTS-v3-Turbo`, Apache 2.0,
`pip install vieneu`) after the user asked for a more natural female voice:
14 built-in preset voices (7 male/7 female, 3 regions, 3 styles), ONNX/CPU
backend (torch-free, lighter than the MMS setup), but natively 48kHz --
NOT 16kHz, so `tts/app.py` resamples down with `soxr` (already a
transitive vieneu dep) before returning, keeping the firmware's fixed-rate
Opus decoder contract unchanged. `MmsTtsClient` renamed `VieNeuTtsClient`.
Model files (ONNX graphs + MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer-Nano-ONNX codec, exact
filenames read from vieneu's own `onnx_runtime_lite.py` source, not
guessed) are host-downloaded via `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download(...,
cache_dir=...)` (`tts/download_vieneu_model.py`) into `tts/vieneu-hf-cache/`,
bind-mounted with `HF_HUB_CACHE` pointed at it -- same in-container
CDN-egress workaround as `asr/`, but using hf_hub_download's own cache
layout instead of a flat directory, so the container's calls find it
without needing `cache_dir` threaded through vieneu's own internals.
`SystemSettings.TtsSpeakingRate` (VITS-only, no native rate control in
VieNeu-TTS) was replaced by `TtsVoice` (preset id, default "Trúc Ly" --
natural female) in the same migration pass; `GET /admin/tts-voices`
proxies the sidecar's own `/voices` so the picker can't drift from what's
actually loaded.

Also added an admin-only test page (web console, "Admin test" nav item,
gated same as Devices' isAdmin) with MQTT health check, water/ping command
buttons (endpoints already existed, just had no UI), and STT/TTS/chat test
panels -- STT test can record from the browser mic directly (raw PCM via
Web Audio API + hand-built WAV, not MediaRecorder, since the server only
accepts mono 16-bit 16kHz WAV) or upload a file; TTS test plays back real
synthesized audio; chat test exercises the LLM only (skips STT) and can
persist to a device's real chat history. A separate SuperAdmin-only
"System config" page holds the TTS voice picker (with a "save & preview"
that plays a sample through the real /admin/voice-test/tts endpoint).

**Pending verification, user's own TODO (as of 2026-08-03):** voice-session
auto-relisten (`synora_voice_session.cc` -- after the assistant's reply
finishes, the device auto-restarts listening instead of going idle, so a
conversation continues without another button press; a ~6s silence timeout
with no speech detected falls back to idle without round-tripping the
server). Built and flashed but not yet tested on hardware -- user said
they'd check later. If this comes up again, ask whether it actually worked
before assuming it did.

**Pending hardware test, user's own TODO (as of 2026-08-03): mic/speaker
noise -- is it the software gain bump, or real hardware coupling?** User
reported I2S mic/speaker noise described as "old CRT TV static when there's
no channel" (broadband hiss, not a tonal hum/whine -- ruled out ground-loop
buzz as the primary suspect). Root-cause candidate found in
`no_audio_codec.cc:251-259` (`NoAudioCodec::Read`): the mic read shift was
already changed from stock `>>12` to `>>10` (+12dB / ~4x software gain bump)
to fix under-sensitive mic pickup, per the code's own comment -- "conservative
software gain bump... to test before assuming root cause is hardware." A flat
gain boost amplifies the mic's noise floor right along with real signal, so
this is a strong candidate for the whole "noise" symptom being software, not
EMI/grounding. Test (not yet run, user couldn't test at the time): temporarily
revert `>>10` back to `>>12` (or try `>>11`), reflash, listen. If static drops
to near-silent -> it was the gain bump; keep the noise-floor/gain tradeoff in
mind rather than chasing hardware fixes. If static is unchanged -> gain isn't
the cause, go back to hardware (star-grounding mic/speaker returns separately,
checking MAX98357A SD pin isn't floating, separating mic/speaker wiring from
shared power rail). Copper-tape shielding was discussed but only helps
E-field coupling if grounded, and wouldn't address this gain-floor theory at
all -- don't suggest it as a fix until the gain test rules itself out. If this
comes up again, ask whether the `>>10` vs `>>12` test happened and what the
result was before re-diagnosing from scratch.

**2026-09-19: the `>>10` vs `>>12` test above finally ran, with hard numeric
data instead of "sounds noisy."** Built [[project_vad_playback_test_app]] (a
standalone firmware, `firmware-synora/test_apps/vad_playback_test/`) with raw
rms/min/max mic logging (not just the clamped 0.0-1.0 level) so clipping
could be confirmed without needing the speaker wired up (it wasn't, this
session). Result: at `>>10`, idle/no-one-talking readings were pinned at
`min=-32767 max=32767` (hard int16-rail clipping) almost every single 200ms
sample. Reverted to stock `>>12` (`main/audio/codecs/no_audio_codec.cc`,
both the mono and AEC-reference-interleaved read paths) -- **this measurably
helped** (readings now vary, e.g. `level=0.19` to `1.00` instead of being
locked at `1.00`) but did **not** fully eliminate clipping. However, this
session's test room was independently confirmed noisy (user: "fans, machine
room") and even the pre-button-press "ambient" baseline read high RMS, so
residual clipping at `>>12` is very plausibly just a loud room, not proof of
a remaining hardware fault. **Inconclusive on the hardware-vs-room question
-- retest in a genuinely quiet room before concluding either way.** The
`>>12` revert is applied in `main/` (real firmware) source and was verified
on `vad_playback_test`, but as of this note the **real firmware has NOT been
reflashed with this gain fix yet** -- the device's real firmware still has
whatever the last real-firmware flash carried (AEC reference channel +
playback-task decoupling + drain-settle fix, from earlier the same session,
but pre-dating the gain revert). The device was last left running
`vad_playback_test`, not the real firmware, per explicit user choice ("leave
the VAD test app flashed, don't reflash real firmware yet"). Next session:
reflash real firmware (picks up the gain fix automatically, same shared
source file) before assuming the device is running current code.

# Memory Index

- [Always flutter clean before building](feedback_flutter_build_clean.md) — skipping it causes phantom compile errors in this sandbox
- [Docker egress workaround](feedback_docker_network_egress.md) — some CDNs (e.g. Gradle) hang forever from inside containers; download on host, bind-mount in
- [Firmware greenfield off xiaozhi](project_firmware_greenfield.md) — stop forking xiaozhi-esp32, build own firmware, pull DSP (esp-sr) as component, keep own server
- [BLE off after pairing](project_ble_always_on.md) — reversed 2026-08-02: BLE now turns off once server confirms isPaired via MQTT state, back on if unpaired
- [Synora board/sensor suite](project_synora_board.md) — pin map, GPIO/swizzle gotchas, WiFi StartStation() bug, pending auto-relisten TODO
- [idf.py silently resets IDF_TARGET on -B dir wipe](feedback_esp_idf_target_reset.md) — clobbers sdkconfig to plain esp32, causes confusing esp-sr header errors
- [VAD playback test app](project_vad_playback_test_app.md) — standalone firmware to test button+VAD+playback without the server; currently flashed on the device instead of real firmware

Docker containers in this sandbox (synora project, toan.nguyen@sensolus.com) have restricted/broken egress to at least some external CDNs — observed with `services.gradle.org`'s redirect target hanging indefinitely (confirmed via `curl -4 -L` timing out after the 307 redirect, while a direct un-redirected request returns fine). The HOST process (outside any container) reached the same URL successfully via `python3 urllib.request` in ~1 minute for a ~230MB file.

**Why:** A first-time `flutter build apk` inside `instrumentisto/flutter:latest` silently stalled for 1.5+ hours on a 0-byte `gradle-9.1.0-all.zip.part` — the Gradle wrapper process was sleeping on a dead socket, not actually slow. `docker exec` into the container showed no active TCP connections and the process in state `S (sleeping)`.

**How to apply:** When a Docker-based build step (Gradle, or likely other tools that lazily fetch large distributions from a redirect-heavy CDN) appears to hang with no progress for an unusually long time, don't assume it's just slow — check for a stalled/zero-byte partial download first (`docker exec <cid> bash -c "find /root/.gradle -name '*.part'"` or equivalent). If confirmed stalled, download the file on the **host** instead (test with `python3 -c "urllib.request.urlopen(...)"`, since host `curl` may itself be broken — it was, with a `libcurl.so.4` / `nghttp2` symbol mismatch, unrelated to network). Then place it at the exact path the container's tool expects (for Gradle wrapper: `~/.gradle/wrapper/dists/<version>/<hash>/<file>.zip`, where `<hash>` is deterministic per distributionUrl — a first failed container run will have already created the (empty) hash directory, revealing the exact name to reuse) and bind-mount that directory into the container (`-v ~/.gradle-cache-host:/root/.gradle`) on retry. This resolved a stuck `app/` Flutter APK build in this project.

See also [[feedback_flutter_build_clean]] for another Flutter-in-Docker sandbox quirk in this same project.

**Gotcha, not a rule the user stated, but cost real debugging time in this
session — record it so it isn't rediscovered from scratch.**

When an ESP-IDF project's `-B <build-dir>` is deleted (e.g. to force a clean
rebuild) and `idf.py build` is re-run with no explicit target, `idf.py`
silently regenerates the project-root `sdkconfig` for the **default esp32
target**, clobbering an earlier `esp32s3` selection that had been set via
`idf.py set-target esp32s3`. The project's `sdkconfig` (not just the deleted
build dir) is what actually carries the "chosen target" state between runs.

**Why it matters:** this produced deeply confusing downstream errors — e.g.
espressif/esp-sr's CMakeLists.txt picks its target-specific header/lib
directory (`include/esp32s3/` vs `include/esp32/`) from `${IDF_TARGET}`, so
under the silently-wrong esp32 target the compiler picked headers missing
symbols (`AFE_TYPE_FD`, `AEC_MODE_FD_LOW_COST`, `aec_nlp_level`) that looked
like a version mismatch or stale component cache, when the actual managed
component on disk was correct and complete. Wasted several rebuild cycles
diffing header content before checking `grep CONFIG_IDF_TARGET sdkconfig`.

**How to apply:** whenever wiping a build dir for a non-default-target
(non-plain-esp32) ESP-IDF project, either (a) delete the project's
`sdkconfig` too and pass `-DIDF_TARGET=<target>` on the next `idf.py build`
invocation, or (b) explicitly re-run `idf.py -B <dir> set-target <target>`
before building again. Don't trust an existing `sdkconfig` to "just still
have the right target" after nuking its build directory -- verify with
`grep CONFIG_IDF_TARGET= sdkconfig` first if something inexplicably breaks
after a clean-rebuild.

See [[project_synora_board]] for the board this applies to (ESP32-S3 N16R8).

Always run `flutter clean` immediately before `flutter build apk --release` (or any `flutter build`) in this sandboxed environment, even when `dart analyze` on the same source tree just reported zero issues.

**Why:** Repeatedly observed in the Synora project (`/home/toan/bench/toan/synora/app`): skipping `flutter clean` before a build causes a stale/corrupted incremental kernel-snapshot cache to resurface bogus errors like "The method 'setState' isn't defined for the type '_XyzState'", "Undefined name 'ref'/'mounted'", "getter 'rssi' isn't defined for Object?" — always in the same file(s), always resolved by `flutter clean` then rebuilding. `dart analyze` on the same files reports no issues at all, confirming these are cache artifacts, not real code problems. This has recurred multiple times across different unrelated source changes in the same project, so it's a property of the build cache/environment, not any particular edit.

**How to apply:** Whenever kicking off a `flutter build apk` (or likely any `flutter build` variant) in this environment, chain `flutter clean && flutter build ...` (or run clean as a separate prior step) rather than reusing prior `build/`/`.dart_tool` artifacts. If a build fails with confusing "undefined method/getter" errors on code that otherwise analyzes cleanly, don't debug the source — just clean and rebuild first.

**Superseded 2026-08-02**: the always-on-BLE requirement below (stated
2026-07-23) was explicitly reversed by user decision. Synora now matches the
reference firmware's original behavior: BLE turns **off** once pairing is
confirmed, and back **on** if the device is ever unpaired.

Implemented in the greenfield firmware ([[project_firmware_greenfield]]):
`SynoraMqtt::ApplyIsPaired()` (`firmware-synora/main/boards/common/
synora_mqtt.cc`) parses the retained MQTT `state` topic's `isPaired` field
(published by the server right after `POST /devices/pair` succeeds — see
`Synora.Api/Program.cs`) and calls `BleProvisioning::Deinit()`/`Init()`
accordingly. Deliberately NOT triggered by `BleProvisioning`'s own local
`kActivated` state in `ConnectAndActivate()` — that only means the phone has
an activation code, not that it has actually called `/devices/pair` with it
yet, and the phone still needs the live BLE connection to read that code.
Waiting for the server-confirmed `isPaired:true` avoids that race.

**Gap closed 2026-08-02**: `DeviceActivation` now persists `is_paired` to NVS
(`SetPaired()`/`IsPaired()`, same `synora_dev` namespace as `device_id`/
`activation_code`/`server_url`), set from `SynoraMqtt::ApplyIsPaired()`.
`SynoraBoard`'s constructor reads it right after `Load()` and skips
`BleProvisioning::Init()` entirely for a returning already-paired device.
Unpairing (GPIO0 10s-hold or BLE `control:factory_reset`, both -> `DeviceActivation::Unlink()`+`Reset()`+reboot)
implicitly clears the persisted flag too, since `Reset()`'s `EraseAll()` wipes
the whole `synora_dev` namespace — so the next boot always finds `is_paired`
back at its default `false` and brings BLE up again. Confirmed via
`docker run espressif/idf:v6.0.2 idf.py build` (clean, both this and the
initial BLE-off-after-pairing change).

Original always-on rationale (now moot, kept for history): BLE was to stay on
concurrent with WiFi for (1) phone-app control/status over GATT, (2) BLE
beacon/presence, (3) a backup control path when WiFi/cloud is down. All three
are BLE GATT/advertising, so this never needed Classic Bluetooth/a second
radio either way — that part of the analysis still holds if always-on BLE is
ever revisited.

As of 2026-07-23, Synora is moving OFF the xiaozhi-esp32 fork to a **greenfield ESP-IDF firmware**. Rationale established by analysis:

- The current `firmware/` is a squashed vendored snapshot of xiaozhi-esp32 (`upstream` remote = github.com/78/xiaozhi-esp32, HEAD = single "Import" commit). License is **MIT** — copying code into an owned tree is allowed (keep the MIT notice).
- The valuable audio **DSP is NOT xiaozhi's** — it's the Espressif `esp-sr` component (AFE/AEC/NS/VAD/wake word) + `esp_audio_codec`/`esp_audio_effects` (Opus), pulled via `idf_component.yml`. Greenfield just declares these as deps.
- The **server is already Synora's own**: `server/` is a .NET solution (`Synora.Api`, `Synora.Core`, `Synora.Protocol`, `Synora.Voice`, ...). Firmware websocket URL is configurable via `Settings("websocket")`, not hardwired to xiaozhi cloud.

**Keep set** (copy from xiaozhi, the real glue): `audio/audio_service.cc` (mic→AFE→wakeword→VAD→Opus→protocol pipeline) + `audio/engines/afe_audio_engine.cc`.
**Clean ports already exist** to build against: `AudioCodec` (Read/Write), `AudioEngine` (Initialize/Feed + OnWakeWordDetected/OnOutput/OnVadStateChange), `Protocol` (binary wire format `BinaryProtocol2/3`).
**Write-new set**: app/state loop, display+LVGL, OTA, board framework, and the `Synora.Protocol` firmware client matching the server.

**Biggest risk / open item**: firmware↔server protocol contract — the new firmware `Protocol` impl and `Synora.Protocol` must agree on the binary framing + JSON messages.

**Server voice endpoint (decided 2026-07-23 to build BEFORE firmware Phase 2, since Synora.Protocol/Voice were empty stubs and there was nothing for the device to talk to):**
- Contract = the xiaozhi WS protocol (per DESIGN.md): WS-upgrade headers (Device-Id/Client-Id/Protocol-Version/Authorization), JSON `hello`/`listen`/`abort`/`mcp` in, `hello`/`stt`/`tts`/`llm`/`mcp`/`system`/`alert` out, binary Opus frames v2 (16B hdr, BE) / v3 (4B hdr) / raw. Route is `/v1/` (renamed from `/xiaozhi/v1/` on 2026-08-01).
- Implemented + verified (docker `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0`, `dotnet test`, 2/2 pass): `Synora.Protocol` (XiaozhiBinaryFrame codec + ServerMessages/ClientMessages), `Synora.Voice` (VoiceSession, IVoicePipeline seam, VoiceConnectionHandler). Endpoint anonymous for now (device token/activation auth TODO).
- **Real LLM landed 2026-08-01** (DeepSeek, OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API): `LlmVoicePipeline` (registered for all environments, incl. Testing via a swapped-in `FakeLlmClient` so tests don't hit the network) replaced `LoopbackPipeline` in DI. STT is still a stubbed placeholder text (`"[loopback]"` — no real ASR yet), and TTS audio is still an echo of the user's own recording (no real speech synthesis yet) — only the LLM leg (text reply) is real, via `DeepSeekLlmClient`/`ILlmClient`, configured through `Llm` appsettings section + `Llm__ApiKey` env var (`docker-compose.yml`'s `server` service reads `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`).
- **Discussion history landed 2026-08-01**: new `DiscussionMessage` entity (DeviceId/SessionId/UserText/AssistantText/CreatedAt), persisted by `LlmVoicePipeline` after each turn (device resolved via the `Device-Id` header = MAC address, not the Device's Guid `Id` — skips persistence silently if unresolvable). `GET /devices/{id}/discussions` (most-recent-first, up to 100) + a web `Devices.tsx` "Show conversations" section render it.
- **Real ASR (STT) landed 2026-08-02**: new `asr/` service (Python FastAPI + `faster-whisper`, `vinai/PhoWhisper-small` converted to CTranslate2/int8 at container startup). Server: `Concentus` (managed Opus decode) + `ISpeechToText`/`PhoWhisperClient` (+ `FakeSpeechToText` for Testing) wired into `LlmVoicePipeline.OnListenStopAsync` — the transcript is now real, replacing the `"[loopback]"` placeholder everywhere (LLM input, persisted `UserText`, the `stt` message). Verified end-to-end live: real Opus audio published over MQTT → decoded → ASR → real Vietnamese transcript → real LLM reply that responds *to that specific transcript* (not a canned response) → persisted. **Two real bugs hit and fixed getting here** (both worth remembering for any future from-scratch container rebuild of this service): (1) the PyPI `ctranslate2` wheel's native `.so` lacks the correct `PT_GNU_STACK` marking and this environment's kernel refuses to map an executable-stack shared object — neither `execstack` (dropped from Debian trixie) nor this `elfedit`'s `--execstack-clear` (doesn't exist in this binutils version) fixed it; `asr/clear_execstack.py` patches the ELF program header directly (finds `PT_GNU_STACK`, clears the `PF_X` bit) as part of the Docker build. (2) Downloading the `vinai/PhoWhisper-small` checkpoint (~967MB) from inside the container **stalled completely** partway through (silent hang, not just slow) — same class of issue as [[feedback_docker_network_egress]]'s Gradle precedent. Fixed by downloading on the HOST instead (`asr/download_model.py`, has stall-detection + HTTP Range resume, and verifies final size against `Content-Length` since a truncated-but-clean connection close looks identical to success without that check) and bind-mounting `asr/model-src` read-only into the container; `entrypoint.sh` converts from that local mount instead of letting `ct2-transformers-converter` fetch the checkpoint itself. TTS (response audio) is still the only remaining placeholder — real speech synthesis (Piper vi-VN per DESIGN.md) doesn't exist yet, so response audio is still an echo of the user's own recording even though the transcript/reply text are both now real.
- **MQTT migration LANDED 2026-08-01** (both server and firmware sides, see Progress below): the whole device<->server link — telemetry/commands (was REST polling) AND voice/audio (was the `/v1/` WebSocket) — now runs over MQTT via Eclipse Mosquitto (`docker-compose.yml`'s `mosquitto` service, password-file auth regenerated from `MQTT_USERNAME`/`MQTT_PASSWORD` env vars by a custom entrypoint). Topic scheme, all under `synora/devices/{deviceId}/` (deviceId = the server-assigned **Guid**, not MAC — simpler than the old WS endpoint's MAC-based `Device-Id` header lookup): `telemetry` (device pub), `unlink` (device pub), `state` (server pub, **retained**, `{muted, isPaired, schedules}`), `commands/water` + `commands/ping` (server pub, NOT retained — one-shot pulses), `voice/control/up`+`down` (JSON hello/listen/abort/stt/llm/tts), `voice/audio/up`+`down` (raw Opus bytes, no length-prefix framing needed since MQTT already frames each publish). `/v1/` WS endpoint and the REST telemetry/pending-command/schedules-GET/unlink endpoints are gone; `PendingWaterDurationSeconds`/`PendingPing` Device fields dropped (migration). Server: `VoiceConnectionHandler` replaced by `VoiceMqttDispatcher` (sessions in a `ConcurrentDictionary<Guid,...>`, 3-min idle timeout swept every 1 min — no LWT-based presence, disclosed MVP scope reduction) + `Synora.Api/Mqtt/MqttService` (single MQTTnet-based `BackgroundService`, implements both `IDeviceMqttPublisher` and `IVoicePublisher`). `LlmVoicePipeline` unchanged (transport-agnostic, only depends on `IVoicePipeline`/`VoiceSession`). Verified: `dotnet build`/`test` 3/3, `docker compose config` valid.
- **⚠️ Security follow-up needed**: while verifying the compose file (`docker compose config`, which prints fully-interpolated env values), the background agent doing this work reported the **Firebase service-account private key got printed into that tool call's output**. Not exfiltrated anywhere further by the agent, but worth rotating that Firebase service-account key out of caution, and being careful re-running `docker compose config` (or similar env-interpolating commands) without redacting output.

Standalone ESP-IDF project (own build/sdkconfig/partition table, NOT part of
the real firmware build) at `firmware-synora/test_apps/vad_playback_test/`.
Built 2026-09-19 to evaluate local on-device VAD-triggered auto-stop before
investing in changing the real app's press-to-talk design (see
[[project_synora_board]]'s 2026-09-19 entry for what it was used to find).

**What it does:** press the BOOT button -> records mic audio -> esp-sr's AFE
VAD (WebRTC model, no WakeNet packed) auto-stops on silence (or a 15s safety
timeout) -> plays the recording back through the speaker. Also logs raw
`rms`/`min`/`max` (not just a clamped display value) every ~200ms so mic
clipping/saturation can be diagnosed numerically without needing the speaker
wired up.

**Why standalone:** reuses the real firmware's audio codec / AFE engine /
button code directly by relative path (`../../../main/...` in its
`main/CMakeLists.txt`) rather than duplicating them, but has no
MQTT/display/BLE/sensor dependencies -- builds and flashes independently of
the server, useful when the server stack isn't up (was the case this
session: `docker compose ps` in the repo root showed nothing running).

**Gotcha already hit once:** deleting its `-B <build-dir>` without
re-running `set-target esp32s3` silently resets the project's `sdkconfig` to
plain `esp32`, which then makes espressif/esp-sr pick the wrong per-target
header set and throws confusing "AFE_TYPE_FD not declared" errors that look
like a version/cache problem but aren't. See
[[feedback_esp_idf_target_reset]].

**Flashing it REPLACES the real firmware on the device** (single board,
single flash) -- reflash the real firmware (`firmware-synora/`, not this
test_apps project) to get back to normal operation. As of 2026-09-19 the
device was intentionally left running this test app, not the real firmware.

**Update 2026-10-05:** reflashed the real firmware (`firmware-synora/`,
build dir `build2`, `idf.py -B build2 -p /dev/ttyACM0 flash`) back onto the
device, so it is no longer running this test app.
